title: Width
definition: Utilities for setting the width of an element, including fixed widths, percentage widths, and viewport widths.
simpleExplanation: How wide something is. You can use the standard spacing scale (`w-16` for 4rem), fractions (`w-1/2` for 50%), or viewport units (`w-screen` for 100% of your monitor).
realWorldExample: Creating a two-column layout by setting two sibling `div` elements to `w-1/2`.

basic: What Tailwind class makes an element span 100% of its parent's width?
intermediate: What is the difference between `w-full` and `w-screen`?

answers.question: full vs screen?
answers.answer: `w-full` sets width to 100% of the PARENT container. `w-screen` sets width to 100vw (100% of the entire browser window), completely ignoring parent constraints.
